alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list insomnia and related neuropsychiatric symptoms as EFV toxicities and recommend: if on EFV 600mg, lower to 400mg; if on EFV 400mg, reassure, and if symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG. Patient started TDF+3TC+EFV in February 2024 and now reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. EFV is a well-established cause of these symptoms. No alternative cause is evident from the clinical notes, though anxiety or other psychosocial factors could contribute. The clinician's plan documents the complaints but does not include any management step such as dose reduction or substitution.

evidence.recommended_action: If on EFV 600mg, reduce to 400mg. If already on 400mg, reassure and if symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG (or ATV/r if DTG contraindicated).

alerts.title: Missing TDF renal monitoring baseline and ongoing
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR at baseline before initiating TDF-based ART. Patient is on TDF but no renal function labs appear in the record. Without a baseline or follow-up creatinine/eGFR, TDF-related nephrotoxicity cannot be detected. The clinician's plan does not include any renal monitoring orders.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR to establish baseline and ongoing TDF renal safety monitoring.

alerts.title: Viral load 60 copies/mL: low-level viremia not addressed
alerts.message: Guidelines define viral suppression as plasma VL ≤200 copies/mL. Patient's last VL was 60 copies/mL on 2025-08-10, which is technically suppressed. However, guidelines acknowledge low-level viremia as a concern for subsequent virologic non-suppression. The clinician's plan does not document recognition of this low-level value or enhanced monitoring. No repeat VL is ordered despite the potential risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Document low-level viremia recognition and ensure next routine VL is performed on schedule per adult monitoring algorithm.
